summary: Tested the 4 fixes (A image links, B journal delete confirm in preview, C account data isolation, D 'Date Not Set') on backend (pytest, 13 tests) and the Expo web preview (390x844). A: Unsplash direct link and Google imgres link both show a preview. 'abc' shows a red hint (rgb 248,113,113). An unreachable https link shows the 'Couldn't load image' fallback. A saved link shows on the card. D: a vision with no date shows 'Date Not Set' on the card and in the detail modal. A vision with date 2027-06-01 shows 202d. B: the Delete Entry confirm renders inside the preview sheet. Cancel keeps the sheet open, Delete removes the entry and closes the sheet. Offline shows 'No Internet Connection' and no confirm. C: demo A creates TEST_A_ENTRY, signs out, then delivered@resend.dev (B) signs in via OTP override. B's Journal shows 0 entries and Vision is empty. Local storage has no A data and the owner id is B's. Signing back in as A works without a crash, but A's local data is gone (expected per E1). The backend /api/journal is scoped per user: B cannot list or delete A's entry. Backend: 11/13 pass. The 2 failures come from cdn.pixabay.com itself. The specific Pixabay test asset (tree-736885) returns Cloudflare-cached S3 403 AccessDenied about 70% of the time from the server IP. Another Pixabay CDN image returned 200 on 5 of 5 calls.

minor.issue: The specific Pixabay test asset is flaky: cdn.pixabay.com serves a Cloudflare-cached 403 AccessDenied (s-maxage=5) in 5s windows. Measured from the container with curl and through the proxy: 200 422 422 422 200 422 422 422 200 422. Resolve then returns 422 'That page blocks previews...' and proxy returns 422 'Not an image'. A different Pixabay CDN image (sunset-1373171_1280.jpg) returned 200 on 5 of 5 calls. Cache-busting query params did not help.

A well-formed https link whose host doesn't resolve returns 400 'Please enter a valid image link (http/https).' The user sees that hint under a valid-looking https URL. Cause: _public_http_url() returns False when getaddrinfo fails. DNS failures should return 422 'That link couldn't be reached.', and the 400 should be kept only for a bad scheme or a private IP.

issues: The 'Couldn't load image — use a direct image link' text (c.textSubtle, xs) sits under the dark bottom gradient (rgba 0,0,0,0.85) and the category pill, so it is barely readable. Render the gradient/pill only when the image actually loads, or raise the contrast of the fallback text.

The copy says 'Your data will remain on this device', but when a different account signs in, all local journals/visions/chat are wiped. With the cloud sync shim being a no-op, A's data is lost for good (verified: A signs back in and sees 0 entries). Change the copy or warn the user.
User B (delivered@resend.dev, name Maya) shows 'Beautiful Soul' / 'BS' because the @hera_user profile is wiped and not re-fetched from the server profile.

action_items: Images: in /api/images/resolve and /api/images/proxy, retry a 403 from the upstream image host 2-3 times with about 2s backoff (Pixabay's CDN cache returns 403 in 5s windows). Alternatively, for a Google imgres link whose decoded URL has an image extension, return the decoded URL even if the server-side check gets a 403, so the client can try loading it directly.
Images: return 422 'That link couldn't be reached.' (not 400 'valid image link') when DNS lookup fails in _public_http_url.
Vision form: make the 'Couldn't load image' fallback readable. Don't draw the dark gradient or category pill over the error state.
Profile: change the Sign Out copy ('Your data will remain on this device'), because an account switch wipes local data. Consider re-fetching the server profile (name) after the switch.
syncService.ts:117: send target_date: v.targetDate || null rather than an empty string, in case a real backend has a date column.

Add testIDs to the journal preview trash/confirm buttons, the Vision '+' button, the form inputs and the cards. There are currently none in journal.tsx or vision.tsx, so tests rely on aria-labels and coordinates.
critical_code_review_comments: vision.tsx (972 lines) is over 700 lines. Split VisionImage, VisionFormModal and the detail modal into separate modules.
journal.tsx:241 handleDelete (list-card trash) still uses showAlert, which is a Modal at the root. That is fine for the list. The preview sheet uses the new in-sheet confirm.
HeraContext applySession: wiping on owner mismatch works. Because sync is a no-op, the previous account's local data is lost for good. This is a product decision, but make it explicit to the user.
Offline alert (template/ui/context.tsx) is a separate RN Modal shown over the journal detail Modal. It stacks correctly on web. iOS stacking of two Modals could not be checked in the web preview.

SSRF guard is good: blocks loopback/private/link-local and a Google imgres link wrapping 127.0.0.1. However, follow_redirects=True does not re-check redirect targets against private IPs (redirect-based SSRF). Use an httpx event hook to validate each redirect hop.

success_rate.backend: 85% (11/13; the 2 failures are the flaky upstream Pixabay CDN asset)
success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested flows (A, B, C, D) pass; 3 minor design/copy issues

seed_data_creation: None in DB. The backend isolation test creates TEST_A_ISO on demo and deletes it by id. UI entries were local only (fresh browser contexts). OTP override for delivered@resend.dev via tests/otp_override_watcher.py (watcher killed afterwards).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login: localStorage hera_onboarded='"true"', /login, demo@heraapp.com + password field '1234'. A brand-new email shows 'Account Not Found' and goes to onboarding, so use delivered@resend.dev for user B: run `python tests/otp_override_watcher.py delivered@resend.dev 4321 400 &` and fill input[placeholder='• • • •']. Journal preview trash: [aria-label='Delete entry']. Profile sign out: get_by_text('Sign out').first, then .last in the alert. Vision + at (344,33). Image URL input: placeholder 'https://images.unsplash.com/...'. The tree-736885 Pixabay asset is flaky upstream; use sunset-1373171_1280.jpg for stable tests.
rca_of_issue: Pixabay failure RCA: running curl from the container directly against cdn.pixabay.com returns HTTP 403 with content-type image/jpeg, but the body is S3 XML AccessDenied, cf-cache-status HIT, s-maxage=5. Cloudflare caches the origin's 403 for 5s windows, so the backend sees the same failures. The backend code is correct; add a retry with backoff to mitigate.
